pages.text: At dusk, Aboagyewaa and her grandmother sat on low wooden stools at the edge of their farm. “Hush,” said Grandma softly. “Tonight we will not talk. Tonight we will listen.”
sentences: At dusk, Aboagyewaa and her grandmother sat on low wooden stools at the edge of their farm.
pages.alt: Aboagyewaa in her green cardigan and Grandma in her blue-and-green cloth sitting side by side on low wooden stools at the peaceful edge of a Ghanaian farm under a warm orange-and-indigo sunset sky.

pages.text: First came the frogs: “Croak, croak.” They were calling from the wet bank by the stream. Aboagyewaa held up one finger. “One sound,” she whispered.
sentences: First came the frogs: “Croak, croak.” They were calling from the wet bank by the stream.
pages.alt: Two small green frogs calling on wet stones beside a gentle farm stream at twilight while Aboagyewaa sits beside Grandma holding up one finger clearly and smiling quietly.

pages.text: Next came the crickets: “Tri-tri-tri.” Tiny insects were singing together in the tall grass. Aboagyewaa held up two fingers. “Two sounds,” she whispered.
sentences: Next came the crickets: “Tri-tri-tri.” Tiny insects were singing together in the tall grass.
pages.alt: Tiny brown crickets chirping on blades of tall green grass in the foreground while Aboagyewaa sits peacefully beside Grandma holding up two fingers clearly.

pages.text: Then came a soft “Hoo, hoo” from a tall tree. An owl was awake! Many animals come out at night to hunt or look for food, and the owl was one of them. Aboagyewaa held up three fingers.
sentences: Then came a soft “Hoo, hoo” from a tall tree.
Many animals come out at night to hunt or look for food, and the owl was one of them.
pages.alt: A spotted brown owl perched on a leafy tree branch against the deepening blue dusk sky while below Aboagyewaa looks up beside Grandma holding up three fingers clearly.

pages.text: A small fruit bat glided silently over the mango trees. Aboagyewaa could not hear a sound, yet she watched its dark wings cross the twilight sky in search of ripe fruit. She held up four fingers.
sentences: A small fruit bat glided silently over the mango trees.
Aboagyewaa could not hear a sound, yet she watched its dark wings cross the twilight sky in search of ripe fruit.
pages.alt: A small gentle fruit bat gliding across the violet-blue twilight sky above ripe mango trees while Aboagyewaa watches in wonder beside Grandma, holding up four fingers clearly.

pages.text: Aboagyewaa smiled. “The forest is not asleep. It is listening and speaking.” Grandma nodded. “That is why we care for it, and why we walk home together before full dark.” Hand in hand, they walked safely home.
sentences: It is listening and speaking.” Grandma nodded.
“That is why we care for it, and why we walk home together before full dark.” Hand in hand, they walked safely home.
pages.alt: Aboagyewaa and Grandma walking hand in hand along a warm footpath toward their lantern-lit village house under the first twinkling evening stars.
